speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I am here to evaluate the skin lesions you are presenting with. Can you describe the appearance of these lesions and tell me when you first noticed them?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the papules described as firm, flesh-colored, and having a central dimple or umbilication? I need to confirm if they have a "pearly" appearance typical of certain viral infections.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of pearly, umbilicated papules in a 2-year-old is highly suggestive of Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
